<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD is a routine AUR packaging script for the GTK4 IPTV player "syn-iptv." The metadata, dependency list, and structure are all standard.

The `source` array fetches a release tarball from the project's own upstream repository (github.com/manupernas/SYN), which is exactly the expected source. The tarball has a real SHA-256 checksum populated (not SKIP), so its integrity is verified.

The `package()` function runs `packaging/stage-native.sh` from inside the upstream tarball to stage the application files into `$pkgdir` and installs the LICENSE. This is the upstream project's own packaging/installation script performing normal file installation — consistent with ordinary packaging practice.

I found no evidence of malicious behavior: no unexpected network requests or downloads from unrelated hosts, no `curl`/`wget | bash`, no obfuscation or encoded blobs, no `eval` of decoded content, and no data exfiltration or system tampering. The Spanish comment simply notes that a helper script replaces SKIP with the real SHA-256, and the checksum is indeed populated with a concrete hash.
</details>
<evidence>
